standard_prerequisites: Context span 680-727: R = k[t, z_1, z_2, ..., w_1, w_2, ..., x]/(z_i t - x^i w_i, z_i w_j); every element has a unique canonical form f = sum_{i=0..d} f_i x^i with f_i in k[t, z_i, w_j] avoiding the products z_i t and z_i w_j; f in (x^n) iff f_i = 0 for i < n; so x is a nonzerodivisor and the intersection of the (x^n) is 0

The (x)-adic completion R^wedge consists of unique infinite sums f = sum_{i>=0} f_i x^i (Algebra, hathat-finitely-generated); the element f = sum_{i>=1} x^i w_i lies in (t, x^n) for every n because x^m w_m is in (t); the claim f not in (t) is proven by the replacement rules for multiplying t g in canonical form (a term of g_0 involving z_i contributes c w_i to f_{l+i}; picking n with z_n absent from the polynomial g_0 leaves w_n absent from f_n, a contradiction)
Algebra, quotient-complete: a quotient of a complete ring is complete iff it is classically complete, so R^wedge/(t) is not complete
core_obligations: R is (x)-adically complete by the context canonical-form analysis and Algebra, hathat-finitely-generated, and (x) is a principal ideal
J = (t) is a principal ideal of R

The context element f = sum x^i w_i lies in every (t, x^n), so its image in R/J lies in the intersection of the powers of (x) mod J, but f is not in (t) = J; hence R/J is not (x)-adically complete (the context conclusion via Algebra, quotient-complete)

Verify completeness of R from the canonical forms in the context
Conclude noncompleteness of R/J from the context element f
